----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATED THE MODELS

A Chat contains multiple Message documents.
Each Message references its Chat and sender.
The Chat model keeps track of its users and the latest message.

CHAT MODEL :-
Purpose: Represents a chat between users.
Fields:
    users: Array of user IDs (ObjectId). References the User model.
    latestMessage: Stores the ID of the most recent message (ObjectId). References the Message model.

Message Model (messageModel.ts)
Purpose: Represents an individual message sent in a chat.
Fields:
    sender: User ID (ObjectId) of the message sender. References the User model.
    chat: Chat ID (ObjectId) where the message was sent. References the Chat model.
    content: The actual text of the message (string)

SERVICES
Purpose:
Defines the business logic operations for the admin module.
Methods:
High-level actions like verifying users, blocking/unblocking, getting user/bike/order/feedback details.
Methods may combine multiple repository calls, apply business rules, or handle data transformation.

repository
Purpose:
Defines data access operations for the admin module.
Methods:
Low-level CRUD operations: fetch, update, delete, and query database entities (users, bikes, orders, feedback).
No business logic—just direct interaction with the database.

WINSTON package
---------------
using winston we send log data to file,http,console
The code you provided sets up a logging system using the winston logging library in a Node.js application. This is commonly used in backend development to manage logs effectively — for debugging, auditing, or monitoring application health.

import { createLogger, format, transports } from 'winston';
This line imports the required functions from the winston package:
createLogger: Function to create a logger instance.
format: Provides formatting tools (like timestamping, customizing log message structure).
transports: Determines where and how logs are saved (console, file, HTTP, etc.).

level: 'info'
This sets the minimum log level to 'info'.
Log levels in Winston (priority from highest to lowest severity):
error
warn
info ← 🟢 Starts logging from here
http
verbose
debug
silly

So only logs at level info, warn, error, etc., will be logged. Lower levels like debug or silly are ignored unless you reduce the level.

🔹 format: format.combine(...)
This configures the format of log messages using multiple formatting functions chained together via combine.

🔸 format.timestamp({ format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' })
Adds a timestamp to each log entry using the specified format (Year-Month-Day Hour:Minute:Second).

🔸 format.printf(...)
Customizes how the log message appears in the output (console or file).

This function gets access to the level, message, and timestamp, and returns a string like this:
[2025-07-20 13:45:12] INFO: Server started successfully
It uses:

return `[${timestamp}] ${level.toUpperCase()}: ${message}`;
🔹 transports: [ ... ]
This is an array that defines where logs are sent or stored.

1️⃣ new transports.Console()
Logs will be displayed on the console (e.g., stdout). Useful for local development and debugging.

2️⃣ new transports.File({ filename: 'logs/error.log', level: 'error' })
Logs with level error only will be written to logs/error.log.
If an error occurs, this file will contain entries like:
[2025-07-20 13:50:01] ERROR: Database connection failed

3️⃣ new transports.File({ filename: 'logs/combined.log' })
Logs with level info and above will be written to logs/combined.log. This includes:
info
warn
error
Note: This file includes all logs except those filtered out by level.

✅ export default logger;
Exports the logger object as the default export, so it can be imported and used in other files:
import logger from './logger';
logger.info('Server started');
logger.error('Something went wrong');
✅ Summary (What It Does)
Creates a logger with structured log messages like:
[2025-07-20 13:30:00] INFO: User logged in
Logs:
All levels from info and above to logs/combined.log
Only error level to logs/error.log
Everything to the console as well

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
POJO stands for:
Plain Old Java Object
It refers to a simple Java object that:
Is not bound by any special restriction.
Doesn’t extend or implement any special classes, interfaces, or annotations from a framework (like Spring, EJB, etc.).
Is used to store data (like a model or entity class).
Has private fields, with public getters and setters.
